title: baseline and approval history still require manual conformance repair

human_turns.quote: If there is no change, then historically they are built and green, which means we don't need to touch them. So the fact that they show up as red Which is unproposed makes me feel like they existed in code without going through the proper approval process and they were just created. So anything that has been approved explicit, even in historical needs to be green.

body:
_Occurrences: S2:H7, S2:H10, S19:H6, S20:H4; corroborating notes: `slice-2-rotation.md`, `slice-12-performance-diagnostics.md`._

The human first reported that existing `red_grid.json` was implemented but appeared as red/unplanned work (S2:H7), then asked why unproposed items and existing functions were absent from the plan (S2:H10). The same complaint returned as “the plan isnt coherent” and “all red” in S19:H6, and as “missing a bunch of details on files and functions and showing unplanned again” in S20:H4. This is not just render churn: proposal revision 1 explicitly says that the baseline comparison omitted uncommitted map and movement files, so valid existing work was reported as unplanned. The render-count finding already deferred in `deferred.json` is treated here only as corroboration; this finding is the unresolved history carry-forward mechanism. The human had already rejected the earlier symptom-level finding, saying its solution was wrong because “there is a historical state that was not carried forward” (`docs/retro/accepted.json`, 2026-08-18).

**Proposed kit/process change** — add a durable slice ledger derived from the last approved baseline, committed history, and the current working-tree delta. Have conformance classify every authored path as carried-forward, new, modified, removed, or omitted, and attach the relevant prior approval/revision to the rendered module, file, and function entry. Make one `proposal doctor` preflight produce schema, baseline, conformance, and hosted-plan diagnostics before rendering; do not rely on the builder to copy an inventory into each new proposal.

**Confidence** — high: four human occurrences across three sessions, a prior rejected fix, seven recorded revisions, and 21 plan renders point to one missing history mechanism.
**Cost** — high: durable state/schema, conformance classification, renderer changes, migration, and regression tests.
**Mechanically checkable** — yes. A test can compare the ledger against `git diff <baseline>`, require a classification for each authored path, and assert that the rendered plan contains no unexplained unplanned item.
